content: 1. Eslcarbazepine acetate reduces the levels of doxycycline by enhancing its metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 2. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 3. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, and caution and close monitoring are recommended. 4. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, and caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Ethanol reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its elimination. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 6. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, and caution and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Ethotoin reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 8. Ferric citrate decreases the levels or effects of doxycycline by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. It is recommended to administer doxycycline at least 1 hour before ferric citrate. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Ferric maltol decreases the levels or effects of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. If no alternative is available, separate administration by at least 4 hours. 10. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Ferrous gluconate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Ferrous sulfate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Doxycycline increases the effects of fondaparinux through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 14. Fosphenytoin reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 15. Doxycycline increases the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 16. Iron dextran complex decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Iron sucrose decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Isotretinoin and doxycycline are contraindicated due to an unknown mechanism that increases the risk of pseudotumor cerebri. Close monitoring is required. 19. Lanthanum carbonate decreases the levels of doxycycline by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer oral tetracycline antibiotics at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. This interaction applies only to oral tetracyclines. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 20. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, and caution and close monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 21. Magnesium chloride decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Magnesium oxide decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Magnesium sulfate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Magnesium supplements reduce the levels or effects of doxycycline by forming an insoluble complex that reduces drug absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 4 hours after tetracycline. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, and caution and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Doxycycline increases the levels of methotrexate by decreasing its elimination. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tetracyclines may reduce intestinal absorption of methotrexate or interfere with its enterohepatic circulation by inhibiting bowel flora and suppressing bacterial metabolism of the drug. 29. Methoxsalen and doxycycline may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and close monitoring are advised due to additive photosensitizing effects. 30. Doxycycline and methoxyflurane should not be co-administered due to pharmacodynamic synergism, which increases the risk of nephrotoxicity. Use an alternative drug. 31. Doxycycline and methyl aminolevulinate may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased photosensitizing effects. 32. Doxycycline decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota. 33. Mipomersen and doxycycline may increase each other's toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 34. Doxycycline decreases the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 35. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of niacin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 36. Doxycycline and ospemifene may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Doxycycline decreases the effects of oxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 38. Oxcarbazepine reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 39. Doxycycline and palovarotene should not be co-administered due to the risk of benign intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) associated with systemic retinoid use. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Doxycycline increases the effects of pancuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 41. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 42. Doxycycline decreases the effects of penicillin G aqueous by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Doxycycline decreases the effects of penicillin VK by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Pentobarbital reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Doxycycline increases the effects of phenindione through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 46. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Phenytoin reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 48. Doxycycline decreases the effects of piperacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 49. Polycarbophil decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Polysaccharide iron decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Doxycycline and porfimer may enhance each other's photosensitivity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Primidone reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Doxycycline increases the effects of protamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 54. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 55. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine (antidote) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 56. Doxycycline increases the effects of rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 57. Rifabutin reduces the levels of doxycycline by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 58. Doxycycline increases the effects of rocuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 59. Rose hips decrease the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. 60. Doxycycline decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 61. Doxycycline increases the levels or effects of siponimod by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of siponimod with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is not recommended. 62. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours. 63. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours. 64. Doxycycline decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. These agents also decrease the levels of doxycycline by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Take doxycycline at least 2 hours before and not less than 6 hours after administration of these agents to avoid magnesium chelation. 65. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 66. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 67. Strontium ranelate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. It is contraindicated. Suspend strontium ranelate during antibiotic therapy. 68. Doxycycline increases the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 69. Sucralfate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 70. Sucroferric oxyhydroxide decreases the levels of doxycycline by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Do not administer at the same time; take doxycycline at least 1 hour before sucroferric oxyhydroxide. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Doxycycline decreases the effects of temocillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 73. Doxycycline and tretinoin are contraindicated due to an unspecified interaction mechanism that increases toxicity. Avoid co-administration. 74. Doxycycline and tretinoin increase each other's levels through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to increased phototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 75. Doxycycline and topical tretinoin increase each other's phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 76. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may reduce the bioavailability of tetracyclines; administer tetracycline at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium. Use alternatives if available. 77. Tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 78. Doxycycline decreases the effects of the typhoid vaccine live by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 79. Doxycycline increases the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression.
